title: Class 3: More personalities, more skills

series.title: Physical AI Lab: Build a Robot Desk Assistant (5 classes)

summary: All voice studio, no glue. Give your robot several personalities it can switch between when you ask, then choose its skills from a menu of real function calls: plan a Muni trip with live arrival times, set timers, remember notes, look things up, roll dice, check the weather and hear about Deepgram's next event.
detail: Your robot already has one personality. Tonight it gets more: each profile has its own name, personality, first line and voice, and you can say "switch to Arnie" mid-conversation and it changes on the spot. Then you pick its skills. Each one is a function call: the agent decides when it needs one, your page runs it and hands back a real answer. Ask how to get to the Ferry Building and it tells you which Muni bus to catch, where, and when the next one comes. Finish by giving your robot a job that mixes the right personality with the right skills.
outcome: A robot with several personalities you can swap by voice, and the skills you picked, answering with real data instead of guesses.
artifact: A multi-personality talking robot with the attendee's chosen function-call skills.
prereqs: Your robot from Class 2, and your laptop with Google Chrome.
Know a few places you go in San Francisco: you'll ask your robot how to get there.

slides.title: Class 3: More personalities, more skills
bullets: Tonight is all voice studio.
First: more personalities, and switching between them by voice.
Then: skills. Real function calls that answer with real data.
slides.note: No hardware changes tonight. If anyone's robot isn't working, send them to the helper table first so they don't miss the studio time.

slides.title: A robot with more than one personality
bullets: Under Profile, press Add a profile: start from a starter (like Arnie) or A blank one.
Give it a Robot name, a Personality, a First thing it says and its own Voice.
Make the two as different as you can: grumpy and cheerful, fast and slow.
Start talking and say: switch to (its name). It changes voice and personality on the spot.
slides.note: Switching is a function call too: the robot calls switch_profile and the page swaps its personality and voice live, without hanging up. Remove this profile deletes the one you're on, so check before pressing.

slides.title: What a function call is
bullets: You describe a function to the agent: its name, what it does, what it needs.
When the conversation calls for it, the agent asks your page to run it.
Your page does the real work: asks Muni, sets a timer, saves a note.
The answer goes back to the agent, and it says it in its own voice.
slides.note: Two minutes. Show the Tool lines in the transcript and the Code panel: the skills you tick become the functions in the agent's settings.

slides.title: Pick its skills
bullets: Open Skills (function calls) and tick the ones you want:
Check the weather · Deepgram events in San Francisco · Timers
Remember notes · Plan a Muni trip · Look things up · Dice, coins and picking
Each one you tick shows a Try: line. Say it and watch the Tool lines.
slides.note: Fewer skills keep a robot focused. Push people to choose what fits their robot, not tick everything. Notes are kept in that browser only. Look things up uses Wikipedia, and says so when there's no article instead of guessing.

slides.title: Where to, and which bus?
bullets: Tick Plan a Muni trip.
Ask: how do I get to the Ferry Building?
It tells you the line, where to catch it, which way it's heading, and when the next one comes.
Trips start from The Hub at 505 Howard, unless you say where you're starting from.
slides.note: Live arrival times come from 511.org; stops and routes come from Muni's published timetable. Short trips get "just walk". The credit line under the skills list is required by Muni's data licence; leave it there.

slides.title: Give it a job
bullets: Pick a job: Hub concierge, study buddy, game-night host, commute helper.
Write a profile for that job, and tick only the skills it needs.
Tell it, in its personality, when to use each skill.
Test it with a partner playing someone who needs help.
slides.note: Good pairs: a commute helper with Muni and the weather; a game host with dice and timers; a study buddy with look-ups, notes and timers.

slides.title: Show a skill off
bullets: Swap robots with your neighbour: switch it to a personality and ask it something useful.
Film your best function call and share it with #RobotLunchLab.

slides.title: Class 4: go wireless (or keep decorating)
bullets: Want it to run with no laptop? Bring a Raspberry Pi 4 or 5 and a battery pack. The setup steps are on the Class 4 page.
No Pi? Come anyway: decorate more and keep tuning your robot.
slides.note: Send the Class 4 page to anyone thinking about the Pi now, so they set it up at home before they come.

flow.title: Your robot's voice studio
flow.note: Connect your robot, then work through Profile and Skills (function calls) in the voice studio.

troubleshooting: It won't switch personality: say the profile's Robot name clearly, and check the profile has a name.
It makes up an answer instead of using a skill: check the skill is ticked, then ask more directly ("check the weather in Paris").
Muni says it can't find a place: give a street address or a well-known place in San Francisco.
Muni gives a line but no time: the live feed didn't answer. It suggests the Muni app instead; try again in a minute.
A timer didn't go off: timers only run while this page is open and the robot is connected.
Its notes are gone: notes are kept in this browser. A different laptop or browser starts empty.
Connect robot does nothing at all: you're not in Chrome. Open the page in Chrome (or Chromium on a Raspberry Pi).
Another program is using the port: quit Thonny and close other tabs with this page, unplug the Pico, plug it back in, and connect again.

The page says the robot reset while talking: a servo is pulling power from the Pico. Check every red wire goes to the + row, the power lead is in a charger or power bank, nothing is on pin 40, and the ground jumper to pin 23 is in.
It cuts you off: raise Patience. It's slow to answer: lower it.
It talks to itself, or stops mid-sentence for no reason: it's hearing its own voice. Switch off Let me interrupt it (barge-in), or move the laptop away from the robot's speaker.
Deepgram stopped the session: check the key was pasted whole, and that the account has credit.
